title: Workflow Automation audit logs: the customer audit search, what it records, and how the SDKs read it

prose.text: Workflow Automation's admin audit trail is a search API, listed with the other products' audit paths in [[shared.audit-logs]]. {{what-recorded}}

prose.label: Paging.
prose.text: {{page-params}} The Go client shares the incident pager, with its page-start and page-size differences: [[zwa.api.incidents-wire:page-start]], [[zwa.api.incidents-wire:page-size]].

prose.label: SDK models.
prose.text: {{python-model}} Go types the before and after values differently from the contract {{divergence:row-json-type}}.

prose.label: Retention and export.
prose.text: Retention is not documented for Workflow Automation, as for several other products: [[shared.audit-logs:other-retention]]. Whether the log can be streamed anywhere is open {{gap:retention-and-streaming}}, and so is whether the API's module and resource filters accept the strings the page lists {{gap:filter-values}}; whether the page's Admin ID is the record's `changedBy` is open too {{gap:admin-id-changed-by}}.

checks.do: Whether a Python caller needs changedAt, changedBy or the before and after values, which the Python model does not expose.
Whether a Go audit search error is a decode failure on oldRowJson or newRowJson.

page-scope.statement: The Audit Logs page (Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Workflow Automation) records the actions admins perform in Workflow Automation and the actions that occur through the Workflow Automation APIs.

quotes: The Audit Logs page records and displays the actions that every admin performs in Workflow Automation and the actions that occur through the Workflow Automation APIs.
On the Audit Logs page (Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Workflow Automation), you can do the following:

page-filters.statement: The Audit Logs page takes a date range, filters by admin, action, module or resource, and offers search.

quotes: Select a date range for the audit logs displayed.
Filter the audit logs by admin, action, module, or resource.
Search for an audit log.

page-actions.statement: On the Audit Logs page, the potential actions are Delete, Insert, Update and Read.

quotes: Potential actions are: - Delete - Insert - Update - Read

page-modules.statement: On the Audit Logs page, the potential modules are API Keys, CSV Upload, Customers, DLP, Incident, Incident Group, Integrations, Template Mapping and Workflow; Privacy and Security changes under Account Settings appear with the Customers module, and Generate Presigned Link clicks on the Incident Details page appear with the Incident module.

quotes: Potential modules are: - API Keys - CSV Upload - Customers - Changes made to the Privacy and Security section of the Account Settings page appear with this module. - DLP - Incident
- The action of clicking the Generate Presigned Link associated with an incident on the Incident Details page appears with this module. - Incident Group - Integrations - Template Mapping - Workflow

page-resources.statement: On the Audit Logs page, the potential resources are Admin Configuration, API Key, CSV User Data, Customer, Evidence Data, Incident Group, Incident Group Mapping, Integration Configuration, Template Mapping, Workflow Definition and Workflow Definition Mapping.

quotes: Potential resources are: - Admin Configuration - API Key - CSV User Data - Customer - Changes made to the Privacy and Security section of the Account Settings page appear with this resource. - Evidence Data

- The action of clicking the Generate Presigned Link associated with an incident on the Incident Details page appears with this resource. - Incident Group - Incident Group Mapping - Integration Configuration - Template Mapping - Workflow Definition - Workflow Definition Mapping

page-admin-id.statement: The Admin ID column holds the login ID of the admin who performed the action, and displays no value when the admin has a shared login ID.

quotes: Admin ID: The login ID of the admin who performed the actions in Workflow Automation. If the admin has a shared login ID, this field displays no value.

page-change-view.statement: Clicking the View icon next to an audit log entry opens a Change window highlighting the differences between the configuration before and after the change; the icon is not available for Read entries, and Insert, Update and Delete entries can be viewed.

quotes: To view the configuration changes, click the View icon next to an audit log entry.
The View icon is not available for audit logs with a Read action.
The Change window appears and the differences between the pre-changes configuration and post-changes configuration are highlighted.

what-recorded.statement: The audit log search filters by time range and field values and returns audit information for every action admins take in the Workflow Automation Admin Portal and every action made through the APIs; the supported filter fields are Action, Resource, Admin and Module.

expect.description:
Filters audit logs based on the specified time period and field values. The result includes audit information for every action made by the admins in the Workflow Automation Admin Portal and the actions made through APIs. The supported field values are:
  • Action
  • Resource
  • Admin
  • Module
The supported time range values are:
  • Start date and time
  • End date and time

record-fields.statement: Each audit record has `action`, `module` (where the action was performed), `resource` (the audited entity) and `changedAt`, all required, and may carry `changedBy` (the admin), `oldRowJson` and `newRowJson` (the entity's previous and current values, typed as objects) and `changeNote`.

expect.description: The module where the action was performed
The audited entity within the module
The admin who performed the action
The previous value of the audited entity
The current or the updated value of the audited entity
The metadata of the configuration changes that occurred

action-values.statement: The action is one of INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CHECKPOINT and UNDEFINED.

expect.description: The action performed by the admin or APIs

page-params.statement: The audit search takes `page` (minimum 0, default 0), `pageSize` (default 10, no stated maximum) and `pageId`.

expect.description: Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page).

Specifies the page ID of the incident in a multi-paginated response. It is a unique identifier returned in the first search request. You can use the page ID instead of the page number in subsequent search requests for faster and more efficient results.

page-params.conditions: Absence claim (no stated maximum): `jq -c '.spec.paths["/dlp/v1/customer/audit"].post.parameters[] | select(.name=="pageSize")'` on dlp-incidents-workflow-automation-api.json returns the description "Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page)." and the schema `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"default":10}`, with no `maximum`; `grep -c -F 'The maximum page size is 100.'` on the file returns 1, the `/dlp/v1/incidents/search` parameter's description.

python-model.statement: Python's audit model keeps `cursor` and `logs`, and each log entry reads only `action`, `module` and `resource`, so `changedAt`, `changedBy`, `oldRowJson`, `newRowJson` and `changeNote` are not attributes of the parsed result; Go's `AuditLog` struct carries all eight.

quotes: self.module = config["module"] if "module" in config else None
self.resource = config["resource"] if "resource" in config else None
ChangedAt  string `json:"changedAt"`
ChangeNote string `json:"changeNote"`

python-model.conditions: Rests on the whole Logs class at the pin, whose __init__ sets only action, module and resource; the raw response object still holds the other members.

action-list.summary: The help page's list of potential actions has Read and no CHECKPOINT or UNDEFINED, while the contract's action enum has CHECKPOINT and UNDEFINED and no Read.

positions.says: The potential actions on the Audit Logs page are Delete, Insert, Update and Read.

quotes: Potential actions are: - Delete - Insert - Update - Read

positions.says: The contract's action is one of INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CHECKPOINT and UNDEFINED.

action-list.impact: A client that filters or branches on the action cannot tell whether Read entries come through the API, or what CHECKPOINT and UNDEFINED entries show as on the page. Not observed.

row-json-type.summary: The contract types `oldRowJson` and `newRowJson` as objects, while Go declares them as strings.

positions.says: oldRowJson is an object holding the previous value of the audited entity.
Go's AuditLog declares OldRowJSON and NewRowJSON as strings.

quotes: OldRowJSON string `json:"oldRowJson"`
NewRowJSON string `json:"newRowJson"`

row-json-type.impact: If the API sends objects, Go's decoding of an audit page fails with a type error, failing the whole GetCustomerAudit call; if it sends JSON text, Go works and the contract is wrong. Not observed.

retention-and-streaming.title: Retention of Workflow Automation audit logs and whether they can be streamed
retention-and-streaming.detail: The audit log is a pull search. No ZWA source states how long records are kept or whether they can be pushed to a SIEM; ZIA and ZPA audit behavior should not be assumed for it.
retention-and-streaming.blocks: planning audit collection for Workflow Automation

admin-id-changed-by.title: Whether the page's Admin ID and the record's changedBy are the same value
admin-id-changed-by.detail: The page describes Admin ID as the admin's login ID and shows no value for a shared login ID; the contract describes changedBy only as the admin who performed the action. The captured sources do not say whether changedBy is that login ID or what it holds for a shared login ID.
admin-id-changed-by.blocks: correlating API audit records with the console's Admin ID column

filter-values.title: Values accepted by the Module, Resource and Admin audit filters
filter-values.detail: The help page lists the potential actions, modules and resources as displayed in the console, and the contract lists a different set of action values; the contract types module and resource as free strings. The captured sources do not say whether the API's module and resource filters accept exactly the page's strings or in what case, and give no admin values.
filter-values.blocks: writing an audit search filtered by module or resource
